items.title: [The Guardian Global Development] Ebola killed 46 members of one man’s family. Now he is fighting to save the rest
items.content_html:
Six months after the Bundibugyo strain swept through eastern DR Congo, Sylvain Kabona Tibasima is still trying to warn friends and family about the dangers of the virus

The day Birungi Nembe was born in a hospital in Bunia, in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, her mother, Sylvie Bongerize Tibasima, 46, was diagnosed with Ebola. Sylvie died a week later, leaving behind her husband and nine children, including her newborn daughter.

But the little girl had contracted the virus shortly after birth as well. Two weeks later, in early September, her tiny body was placed in a wooden coffin, which was nailed shut and lowered into a small grave by a burial worker dressed in protective gear. Few relatives attended; the risk of infection was just too high.

items.title: [mainichi.jp] Japan's Prime Minister Takaichi presses Putin over detained reporter, seized assets
items.content_html: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi spoke with Russian President Vladimir Putin for about 30 minutes after an APEC welcome dinner in Shenzhen on Nov. 18, the first face-to-face meeting between Japanese and Russian leaders since 2019. Japan said Takaichi raised the detention of Hokkaido Shimbun reporter Yuki Imai and the protection of Japanese companies. The leaders agreed to continue communicating at various levels. Japanese sources said Takaichi called for Imai’s immediate release and urged Moscow to reverse its temporary takeover of Japan Tobacco assets in Russia. Imai was arrested in Sakhalin on Oct. 13 on suspicion of espionage. His current detention period is due to expire Dec. 12 but could be extended. Japan had protested a day earlier after suspected Russian aircraft entered its airspace. The countries also disagree over Ukraine and sovereignty over disputed islands. Russia’s Presidential Executive Office had not publicly confirmed the conversation.

items.title: [theguardian.com] EU proposes extra €45 billion Ukraine loan, faces fight over guarantees
items.content_html: The European Commission proposed on Nov. 18 an additional €45 billion loan for Ukraine in 2027, covering about two-thirds of a projected €70 billion funding gap. It would supplement the €90 billion EU loan already approved for 2026 and 2027; the new package allocates up to €25 billion for military needs and €20 billion for Ukraine’s state budget. Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the funding was intended to strengthen Kyiv’s position in negotiations with Russia. Ukraine would repay the principal only after receiving Russian reparations. The EU would raise the money on capital markets, with its common budget guaranteeing the borrowing. Budget support would be conditional on Ukrainian reforms, including on the rule of law and corruption. The Commission also wants other international partners to cover the remaining €25 billion of Ukraine’s estimated needs. Approval faces resistance from Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Hungary and Slovakia, which have signalled they do not want to join the financing. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has pressed for all 27 EU members to share responsibility and linked the Ukraine financing to talks on the bloc’s next long-term budget; Slovakia’s Prime Minister Robert Fico called that approach “blackmail”. EU leaders are due to discuss the proposal at a Brussels summit on Nov. 26-27, and the budget guarantee requires unanimous member-state backing.

What happened

Four held articles never aired on their focus day

Focus routing released 0 articles and held 4. Two were held for "The Living World" and two for "Maker & Repair", with target release dates of 2026-11-18 and 2026-11-22. None of the four reached an episode on this run. They remain in the queue for their focus days, so the cost to listeners tonight was zero stories from those focus slots, and the cost to the cycle is that the Maker & Repair and Living World weeks will carry a smaller pool than the schedule assumes.

The forestry focus week (cycle week 2 of 4) released nothing from the focus routing itself, so the theme and local material carried the whole episode. Check whether the routing should release a minimum count when the focus day is not the current one.

Eighteen roundup stories kept, twenty-three cut, two deep dives

The roundup pool held 18 stories: 15 theme and 3 local. The airtime budget (NEWS_ROUNDUP_COUNT) dropped 23 from the pool, so the aired segment covered a fraction of what was curated. By design, the cut stories stay eligible for a later day. The deep dive pair was the Quesnel curtailment coverage, with the lead set to local under the Cariboo heading, which is where the debate question on who counts as affected by the curtailment came from.

Of 5 local stories available, 3 aired, and the roundup opened on local material. Citation alignment in the roundup matched 11 of 18, while both deep-dive citations matched. The gap in the roundup is the one to watch: 7 unmatched citations in a segment of 15 planned pairs means some spoken claims are not tied to a source the listener can find.

Change: review the roundup citation matching in the script-assembly step, since 11 of 18 is the weakest number on the page.

The first draft came in 753 words short and the expand pass fixed it

The first draft ran 2547 words against a target of 3400. It was sent back for one expand pass and shipped at 3223 words, which is still under target. Under the rule that a thin day is intended and only matters against SHORT_EPISODE_WORDS, this run is acceptable, but the gap shows the pool was not deep enough to fill the target without the expand pass. Casey's share of the deep-dive words was 48%, and the Casey-to-Riley voice ratio was 0.92, so the two voices stayed close to balanced.

Two TTS takes came back shorter than their word count predicted. Each was retried once, and both retries stayed short. The longer take of each was kept, so no words were dropped from the audio, though the two takes may have been clipped at the source.

Change: if the expand pass is the regular fix for thin days, raise the default pool size so the first draft reaches target without a second pass.

items.title: [The Guardian Global Development] ‘Crocodiles are possible, but hunger is certain’: Malawi’s foragers forced into infested waters
items.content_html:
Once ‘famine food’, empty granaries have forced people along the Shire River to harvest water-lily roots in waters full of the reptiles

The mid-morning heat in Malawi’s lower Shire River basin is already suffocating, but Beatrice Maseko cannot afford to look away from the water’s edge. Coated in grey, foul-smelling mud up to her thighs, the 34-year-old mother of four plunges both arms deep into the heavy sediment of a sprawling marsh. Her fingers feel blindly through the silt for the rough, bulbous roots of wild water lilies, known as nyika.

Around her, a dozen other women move with deliberate, hushed slowness. No one splashes; no one speaks above a tense whisper. Just 50 yards away, where the marsh opens into the main artery of the Shire River, the silhouette of a Nile crocodile glides silently beneath the surface.

The governments say the scheme would comply with EU and international law. The pilot is expected to cover about 100 to 200 people, with the first transfers planned for 2027. The countries argue that sending people to a third country when their country of origin will not take them back could increase removals and deter irregular migration. The proposed facilities would be open, but migrants could remain in Rwanda indefinitely if they cannot be returned to their home countries. Rights groups and legal experts warn that the plan could expose migrants to abuse and leave them without clear ways to challenge decisions. The 2023 UK Supreme Court ruling against a similar Rwanda arrangement provides a legal precedent. The five states are expected to work out detailed terms in early 2027 before launching the pilot later that year.

Moscow suspended vehicle traffic at Narva in February 2024, but pedestrians continued to cross. The decision follows an attempted arson and explosion at Threod Systems, an Estonian maker of reconnaissance and attack drones in Viimsi, near Tallinn. Estonia says Russia’s military intelligence service, the GRU, ordered the attack. Eight residents of Latvia were detained; authorities said company security stopped the attempt before it caused significant damage or injuries. How long the closure will last remains undecided. Interior Minister Igor Taro said Estonian ministers would decide whether it is temporary or indefinite. People from Estonia who are in Russia, along with truck drivers, have been given about two weeks to return before crossing becomes more difficult. items.title: [channelnewsasia.com] ASEAN keeps Myanmar leaders barred, ties return to peace-plan progress
items.content_html: Southeast Asian leaders agreed on Nov. 15 to maintain restrictions on Myanmar’s political leaders’ participation in Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summits and foreign ministers’ meetings, and set conditions for their return. A career diplomat from Myanmar’s foreign ministry represented the country at the Manila summit, rather than its military-backed president or foreign minister. The leaders said restoring full political representation would depend on “sustained and concrete progress” on ASEAN’s Five-Point Consensus, the bloc’s plan to end violence and advance dialogue, mediation and humanitarian aid. They called on the military, security forces and armed groups to stop attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure, and pressed for a nationwide ceasefire and safe aid access. The leaders acknowledged that implementation remains insufficient; Philippine Foreign Affairs Secretary Theresa Lazaro cited ongoing bombings and displacement. The statement also encouraged ASEAN members to engage Myanmar individually, in consultation with the bloc’s chair, while keeping the consensus as the main framework. Leaders did not decide in Manila when Myanmar could return to high-level political meetings; the question is expected to pass to Singapore when it assumes ASEAN’s rotating chair in 2027.
